The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. Sanusi questioned the significance of headline economic figures if poverty, unemployment and hardship remained widespread. He also warned that some economic gains could be vulnerable because of the volatility of foreign portfolio investments, which he said were attracted partly by high interest rates and could leave when market conditions changed. The Emir called for a comprehensive reform programme that went beyond fuel subsidy removal and changes to the foreign exchange regime, emphasising the need for infrastructure, structural reforms, transparency and accountability. He further criticised what he described as the government’s tendency to dismiss public complaints about economic hardship, saying concerns raised by Nigerians should be taken seriously rather than treated as opposition to government policies. Sanusi also raised concerns about regional imbalance in political and security appointments, arguing that the concentration of important positions in particular parts of the country could undermine national cohesion and the perception of fairness. He said Nigeria must promote inclusion and ensure that its institutions and opportunities reflected the country’s diversity. Former President of the African Development Bank, Dr Akinwumi Adesina, called for increased investment in young people, describing Africa’s youthful population as an opportunity for economic transformation. Adesina said young Africans needed access to quality education, healthcare, nutrition, technical skills, finance and digital technology to enable them to establish businesses and create jobs rather than depend solely on paid employment. He cited Nigeria’s telecommunications liberalisation in 2001 as an example of how policy reforms, competition and private sector investment could transform an economy. Tijani said artificial intelligence presented another major opportunity to improve productivity but noted that countries needed adequate connectivity, computing and data infrastructure, skills, research and supportive institutions to benefit from the technology. He also highlighted the Federal Government’s plan to expand broadband connectivity through a proposed 90,000-kilometre open-access fibre network, alongside investments in technical talent development and Nigeria’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. Oteh said African countries must mobilise domestic resources and deepen participation in their capital markets, while equipping young people with the skills needed to participate in the economy. She also identified decentralisation as an important factor in development, citing electricity reforms as an example of how subnational governments could improve power supply and support economic activities. The conference also featured the launch of the inaugural Oxford Global Think Tank (OGTT) Artificial Intelligence Report, which is expected to contribute to efforts to shape Africa’s AI future, strengthen collaboration and position the continent to harness opportunities offered by the technology. item.title: Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, who contested the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District, has insisted that his mandate cannot be taken away from him. Kaura made the assertion while addressing a press conference at his residence in Kaura Namoda, where he claimed that he had been officially declared winner by members of the primary election committee sent by the APC national headquarters. He alleged that the committee’s chairman was taken to an undisclosed location by some individuals he described as anti-democratic elements. According to the senator, the chairman was abducted and subsequently announced a result declaring Senator Sahabi Ya’u winner, but a majority of the committee members rejected the announcement and jointly declared him winner. Kaura described the alleged abduction as an attempt to undermine democracy, insisting that the electorate would not accept such an outcome. He also dismissed the opposing camp’s claim that Sahabi had been declared winner, describing the announcement as invalid. The senator said APC members had turned out in large numbers to vote for him as the party’s candidate for Zamfara North in the 2027 general elections. He thanked the electorate for the confidence reposed in him and urged political stakeholders to respect what he described as the people’s mandate and the result announced by the committee members. item.title: Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was reportedly left distraught and broke down in tears in the dressing room after the accidental collision that preceded the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, with teammates rallying around him to offer support. According to The Sun UK, the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international was seen praying and crying following the incident during Monday’s Segunda División match between Tenerife and Andorra. Owono’s knee struck De Miguel’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball in the closing stages of the encounter. The 30-year-old striker was left motionless on the pitch, prompting distress among players, some of whom were reportedly seen in tears. The goalkeeper was shown a straight red card before the referee abandoned the match in second-half stoppage time. De Miguel was taken to hospital after reportedly suffering a cardiac arrest on the way, with paramedics said to have resuscitated him. Tenerife initially described his condition as “stable but serious” on Monday night, but he died on Tuesday morning. The Sun, citing Spanish newspaper AS, reported that Andorra players showed great concern for Owono during their journey back from Tenerife, with the goalkeeper visibly shaken by the tragedy. Journalist Ivan Alvarez also told COPE radio that Owono had intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before learning of his death. The goalkeeper has reportedly deactivated his social media accounts since the incident and is said to be seeking an opportunity to offer his condolences to the bereaved family before making a public statement. Meanwhile, a judge is expected to open an investigation into De Miguel’s death, although a Canary Islands court source described the incident as an “accidental collision on the playing field”. The source explained that a judicial investigation is automatically opened in cases of deaths not resulting from natural causes, including accidents. Owono is not expected to face criminal sanctions, according to the report, although he could still face sporting disciplinary action. De Miguel’s partner, Maria, and their one-year-old daughter, Carla, were reportedly watching from the stands when the incident occurred. Tenerife have expressed their grief over the striker’s death, while UEFA has announced that a moment of silence will be observed at all its matches this week in his memory. Security sources disclosed that the suspects; Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022, in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State. “The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” disclosed one of the sources. While receiving the four, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, Counsel to the suspects, commended the Service for their relentless efforts towards safeguarding Nigeria’s security, particularly acknowledging the DGSS’ genuine attempt at upholding human rights. item.title: Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Police Command has uncovered a suspected counterfeit dollar printing operation in Odigbo Local Government Area, arresting one suspect and recovering three bags of suspected fake United States dollar notes. The operation followed an investigation into an alleged $6,000 currency fraud involving a businessman in Okitipupa. The police said the case began after Yusuf Nasiru, of Sabo, Okitipupa, lodged a complaint on October 28, 2026, alleging that two men, Peter Desmond and Olami Toro, both from Ode-Irele, approached him at his shop on October 25 to exchange dollars for naira. According to the complainant, he handed over $6,000, valued at about N8.6 million, to the men. However, while waiting for the naira equivalent, the suspects allegedly returned the dollars, claiming they did not have enough money to complete the transaction, before leaving. Nasiru later discovered that the returned notes were counterfeit and reported the matter to the police. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said operatives of the Okitipupa Division commenced an investigation following receipt of the complaint. He said intelligence gathering and technical tracking led the operatives to one of the suspects, Peter Desmond, at Kiniso Village, via Ajue, in Odigbo LGA. “Acting on credible intelligence from community members, operatives raided the hideout on October 29, 2026, believed to be used for producing and printing counterfeit dollar notes to defraud unsuspecting members of the public,” Abayomi said. He disclosed that one suspect was arrested during the raid, while other occupants of the premises escaped through a perimeter fence. A search of the premises, he said, led to the recovery of three bags containing suspected counterfeit US dollar notes and a small wooden box, which had been taken into police custody as exhibits. Abayomi added that the arrested suspect had provided useful information to assist the ongoing investigation. He said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, had directed that the investigation be intensified to apprehend other suspects, establish the full extent of the alleged criminal network and prosecute those found culpable. The command cautioned residents against engaging in suspicious foreign currency transactions with unverified individuals or accepting seemingly attractive exchange offers outside authorised channels. It also advised members of the public to authenticate foreign currencies before accepting them and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. The police assured residents of their commitment to combating financial crimes and protecting lives and property across the state. item.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. item.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
item.description: Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added. Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added. Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban. It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months. Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling. Several countries have indicated an interest in following Australia’s lead, including New Zealand, the UK, France and Turkey. A team of Australia-based researchers published a study earlier this year that found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence of the restrictions.
